evals.name: onboard-to-refunds-repo
evals.prompt: I'm new on the refunds team. Can you walk me through how this repo works? Mostly I want to understand what happens when a support agent creates a refund, end to end.
evals.expected_output: A read-only answer that names all three entry points in pyproject.toml, traces POST /refunds from api.py through handlers, validation and service to the store with correct file and line references, shows that refunds-bulk (src/refunds/bulk.py) is a second way refunds are created that skips the order and over-refund checks the API applies, explains how the worker sends approved refunds to Razorpay including that a failure or timeout leaves the refund approved so it is sent again, and that each process holds its own copy of refunds.json, states that nothing in the repository records orders, and reports where the docs disagree with the code (make run, configuration source, test naming, 'same rules' for bulk). No file in the repository changes.
expectations: No file in the repository was created, edited or deleted and nothing was committed: `git diff fixture --stat` is empty, `git log fixture..HEAD` is empty and `git status --porcelain` is empty (git-ignored __pycache__ from running the repo's own tests does not count; an untracked notes or planning file does)
It names all three entry points declared in pyproject.toml: refunds-api (refunds.api:main), refunds-worker (refunds.worker:main) and refunds-bulk (refunds.bulk:main)

The POST /refunds trace goes from do_POST in src/refunds/api.py through handlers.create_refund, validation.parse and RefundService.create to Store.insert_refund, and every file and line reference given anywhere in the answer points at the code it describes (the grader checks at least three; a wrong file or a line more than five away fails)

It explains that the CSV import in src/refunds/bulk.py writes refunds straight to Store.insert_refund without RefundService, so a bulk refund is never checked against the order existing or against the amount already paid and refunded, and the worker will send it

It points out that docs/refunds.md says the same rules apply to refunds-bulk, which the code contradicts (no over-refund or order check, and bulk holds a refund at or above Rs 5,000 while the API holds only above it)

It explains that the worker sends only refunds with status approved (a refund above the limit is stored as awaiting_approval) and marks a refund sent only after gateway.refund returns, so any OSError including a timeout (urlopen timeout=10 in gateway.py) leaves it approved and it is sent again on the next poll, with no idempotency key, which can refund a customer twice when Razorpay had in fact accepted the first call

It explains that the API and the worker are separate processes that each load refunds.json once into memory (Store.__init__) and rewrite the whole file on every write, so the worker does not see refunds created after it started and one process can overwrite the other's changes

It states that nothing in the repository records orders or paid amounts (Store.add_order is called only from tests), so the paid amounts the over-refund check reads must be written into the JSON file from outside this repository, and it does not invent where they come from

It reports the three doc drifts: `make run` (Makefile line 4) starts the worker, not the API the README says; configuration is read from config.json by src/refunds/config.py, not environment variables (only the Razorpay keys come from the environment, and REFUNDS_DB in .env.example is never read); test files are named *_test.py while CONTRIBUTING.md says test_<module>.py
It does not present anything absent from the repository as fact (no database server, queue, deployment platform, approval screen or authentication layer is described as part of the system)
Neither the final message nor any file the run wrote contains an em dash character (checked on the final message in transcript.md, so a run that wrote nothing is still judged)

evals.name: where-to-change-approval-limit
evals.prompt: Where do we decide whether a refund needs manager approval? Finance wants the limit raised from 5,000 to 10,000 rupees next sprint and I want to know everything I'd have to touch before I estimate it. Don't change anything yet.
evals.expected_output: A read-only answer listing every place the limit lives and the value each needs: MANAGER_APPROVAL_ABOVE in service.py and the 500000 literal in validation.py (1,000,000 paise), REVIEW_FROM_RUPEES in bulk.py (10000, because it is in rupees), the Rs 5,000 message in handlers.py; the three comparisons that disagree at exactly the limit; the tests that would fail, including the two whose amounts stop exercising the large case; the unused approval_threshold_paise key and the docs that say config.json controls it and that bulk follows the same rules; and refunds already awaiting approval.
expectations: No file in the repository was created, edited or deleted and nothing was committed: `git diff fixture --stat` is empty, `git log fixture..HEAD` is empty and `git status --porcelain` is empty (git-ignored __pycache__ from running the repo's own tests does not count; an untracked notes or planning file does)

It names MANAGER_APPROVAL_ABOVE = 500_000 with needs_approval in src/refunds/service.py, the separate literal 500000 that sets the needs_manager flag in src/refunds/validation.py, and APPROVAL_NOTE ('Refunds above Rs 5,000 ...') in src/refunds/handlers.py as places that must change
It names REVIEW_FROM_RUPEES = 5000 in src/refunds/bulk.py as a separate approval decision that must change too, because the CSV import never calls RefundService or needs_approval

It gives the correct new value for each place in that place's own unit: 1,000,000 paise (10_00_000) in service.py and validation.py, but 10000 in bulk.py, which counts whole rupees; an answer that sets every place to one number fails

It points out that the three checks disagree at exactly the limit (service.py uses >, validation.py and bulk.py use >=), so a refund of exactly the limit is auto-approved through the API but held when it comes from the CSV, and it asks or recommends which rule finance wants at exactly Rs 10,000

It names the tests that would fail after the change (by function name or by a file:line inside it): test_threshold_is_exclusive in tests/service_test.py, test_flags_large_refund in tests/validation_test.py, test_rows_become_refunds in tests/bulk_test.py

It works out that two tests stop exercising the large case and need new amounts, not just new assertions: test_large_refund_waits_for_manager uses 600_000 against an order paid 900_000, so a large refund above 1,000,000 needs a larger order in setUp or it hits OverRefund; and the 7500 rupee row in test_rows_become_refunds becomes approved

It states that approval_threshold_paise in config.json is not read by any code (src/refunds/config.py loads only db_path, port, razorpay_base_url and worker_poll_seconds), so editing config.json alone would change nothing, and that docs/refunds.md is wrong both in saying config.json sets the limit and in saying refunds-bulk follows the same rules

It raises what happens to refunds already stored as awaiting_approval between Rs 5,000 and Rs 10,000: the change does not re-evaluate them and nothing in the repository moves a refund out of awaiting_approval
It does not claim the limit is configurable at runtime, or that an approval screen, database or other store exists that the repository does not show
Neither the final message nor any file the run wrote contains an em dash character (checked on the final message in transcript.md, so a run that wrote nothing is still judged)
